authorityMigration.recordedBy: Codex under the founder-authorized complete repository correction
authorityMigration.reason: Replace the brittle whole-GDD hash with a versioned product-to-art projection that invalidates canons only when selected art-relevant GDD sections change.

thesis: A warm, intelligent frontier civilization survives by standardizing what must remain dependable and visibly adapting what history has damaged. Every object is a clear tool first, a record of player ingenuity second, and decorative scenery never.
playerPromise: The player can recognize function, ownership, orientation, danger and state in one second on mobile, then discover a deeper construction history that makes the fortress feel personally authored, repairable, persistent and worth improving with friends.

precedenceContract.identityWins: Salvaged Frontier decides what the world means, remembers and feels.
precedenceContract.disciplineRole: Industrial Toy Defense constrains clarity, thickness, hierarchy, modularity and state readability.
precedenceContract.conflictRule: When narrative texture and immediate comprehension conflict, preserve the Salvaged Frontier meaning through a simpler, thicker and more causal expression instead of importing Industrial Toy Defense motifs.

fromSalvagedFrontier: Purposeful repair history, recovered technology and warm evidence of human intervention.
Controlled asymmetry that explains replacement, reinforcement, sealing or rerouting.
A fortress culture whose objects accumulate memory without losing standardized gameplay anchors.
Material aging caused by impact, heat, contact, ground abrasion or an explicit repair operation.
A hopeful survival tone in which scarcity produces ingenuity rather than misery or visual decay.
fromIndustrialToyDefense: Primary function must be readable from silhouette before surface detail.
Structural volumes remain thick, graspable, modular and visually load-bearing.
Large bevels, protected apertures and explicit joints make construction understandable.
Semantic accents remain bounded, local and redundant with shape, motion and audio.
Repeated assets preserve a calm mass hierarchy and never collapse into visual chatter.
explicitlyRejected: A fifty-fifty visual hybrid or any requirement to make the world literally resemble a construction toy.
Random scrap silhouettes, universal rust, cable spaghetti, micro-greebles and uniform distress.
Pristine molded-plastic surfaces, near-perfect symmetry and cheerful toy color blocking as world identity.
Military realism, photoreal apocalypse, bleak monochrome and anonymous industrial kitbash.
Any salvage detail that weakens function recognition, collision honesty or mobile state readability.

allocationRules: Quiet structural neutrals occupy most visible area so silhouette and state breaks remain dominant.
Sun-baked copper marks player authorship, approved replacement and intervention rather than generic decoration.
Mint interaction light is protected, local and never used as broad surface paint.
Threat raspberry belongs to hostile forward-facing anatomy and never contaminates player-owned structure.
Warning gold and critical red remain below their coverage caps and require non-color shape cues.

surfaceLogic: Player technology uses broad coated structural planes over a dependable standardized chassis.
Replacement modules differ through value, joint language and edge history, not arbitrary material roulette.
Bare metal appears at load paths, hinges, exposed breaks and repair interfaces rather than as global shine.
Rubber and soft protection remain confined to feet, grips, seals, bumpers and vibration contacts.
Wood is reserved for believable low-energy architecture, temporary field structures or biome-specific recovery, never every machine.
wearLogic: Every scar must answer what caused it, when it happened and why it remains visible.
Intact means maintained, not factory-new: one or two old repaired histories may remain without implying current failure.
Damaged states expose one causal weakness; critical states widen the same failure chain.
Wear density decreases with camera distance and may not compete with interaction, threat or state cues.
Repair surfaces are cleaner at the new joint and older away from it, producing readable temporal layering.
forbidden: Uniform rust, full-surface grunge, noisy normal maps and identical scratches on every asset.
More than three visible material families on a normal gameplay prop.
Wooden armor on high-energy machinery without a thermal or structural justification.
Specular-only material identity that disappears under adverse lighting.
Material changes that imitate interaction, danger or team ownership without semantic intent.

worldNarrative.purpose: Make the entire world express intelligent survival, persistence and human authorship.
worldNarrative.deepReason: The GDD makes the fortress a home, workshop, strategy space, social space and museum. A world that visibly remembers repair and adaptation turns progression into identity instead of inventory accumulation.
rules: Civilization appears pressured but capable, organized and future-facing.
Standardized infrastructure proves shared knowledge; local adaptations prove personal history.
Every location contains one legible story of need, response and improved survival.
Hope is expressed through maintenance, warm intervention and active reuse rather than pristine abundance.
failureModes: Bleak post-apocalyptic misery with no evidence of competence or future.
Random salvage decoration that cannot explain a need or a repair decision.
Generic sci-fi frontier visuals disconnected from fortress experimentation.
acceptance: A viewer can describe what the inhabitants protected, repaired or repurposed.
The scene feels inhabited by capable builders rather than abandoned.
The fortress remains the dominant authored protagonist.

silhouetteAndMassing.purpose: Guarantee instant function and distinctive identity at mobile distance.
silhouetteAndMassing.deepReason: Players must act before they can inspect texture. Thick primary masses lower recognition time, while one controlled adaptation landmark gives the object memorable authorship without weakening its gameplay icon.
rules: Primary silhouette carries function, orientation and footprint before any salvage treatment.
Each object owns one dominant silhouette sentence and at most two supporting landmarks.
Negative spaces are few, large and functional.
The authored adaptation modifies a secondary mass or edge rhythm, not the core collision promise.
failureModes: Many equal-sized parts producing a scrap cloud.
Thin antennas, rails or cables becoming essential recognition landmarks.
Asymmetry that changes perceived hitbox, forward direction or ground stability.
acceptance: Black silhouette identifies function and front at the target distance.
Removing tertiary details does not change recognition.
The object remains recognizable in groups of thirty.

constructionAndModularity.purpose: Make every assembly plausible, repairable and reusable as a production system.
constructionAndModularity.deepReason: The game promises experimentation. Visible modules, load paths and service access let players intuit how objects work, while standardized anchors allow many variants without breaking Studio integration or performance.
rules: Seventy-five to eighty-five percent of the visible structure belongs to a stable modular chassis.
Every part connects through a bracket, socket, hinge, clamp, weld, strap or explicit energy interface.
Service access faces the player-safe side and active function faces the threat side.
Shared modules retain scale, bevel family, anchors and naming across variants.
failureModes: Floating plates, unexplained intersections or impossible load paths.
One-off geometry that cannot transfer to another asset family.
Decorative seams and fasteners that imply nonexistent mechanisms.
acceptance: A reviewer can trace load from active mass to foundation.
The object can be decomposed into named stable modules.
A sixth asset reuses the grammar without inventing a new joint family.

asymmetryAndRepair.purpose: Turn asymmetry into a readable record of adaptation rather than visual noise.
asymmetryAndRepair.deepReason: Purposeful asymmetry supplies the emotional identity of Salvaged Frontier, but bounded asymmetry preserves the competence, clarity and repeatability inherited from Industrial Toy Defense.
rules: Every asymmetry is classified as replacement, reinforcement, sealing or rerouting.
Intact player assets target 0.24 asymmetry and never exceed 0.36 globally.
One side may carry the dominant repair story; the opposite side stays visually calmer.
A repair changes local rhythm, value or joint language while preserving pivot, footprint and gameplay anchors.
failureModes: Asymmetry added because an empty area looked boring.
Multiple unrelated patches competing for attention.
Repair details distributed uniformly across the whole object.
acceptance: Each asymmetric feature has a written cause and structural consequence.
Mirror comparison reveals one controlled narrative cluster rather than total disorder.
The object still reads as one standardized family.

materialsAndSurface.purpose: Create tactile richness and history without sacrificing calm shapes or mobile performance.
materialsAndSurface.deepReason: Surface history supports attachment only when it reinforces construction and causality. Material excess would turn persistent identity into noise and create needless texture cost.
rules: Use no more than three visible material families on a normal gameplay prop.
Prefer value-blocked material zones larger than the minimum screen-space band.
Use directional wear at impact, heat, ground, hand and repair interfaces.
Keep broad planes calm enough for bevel light and state breaks to remain legible.
failureModes: Photoreal texture density on stylized proportions.
Full-surface dirt or procedural noise with no causal hierarchy.
Material boundaries smaller than mobile-readable geometry.
acceptance: Material family remains identifiable in all required lighting profiles.
Flat-albedo view preserves the intended hierarchy.
Texture removal does not erase function or state.

paletteValueAndSemantics.purpose: Separate world identity, player authorship, interaction, threat and damage with redundant signals.
paletteValueAndSemantics.deepReason: A warm frontier palette creates emotional ownership, but gameplay colors must remain a strict language. Bounded semantic accents protect accessibility and prevent the world from becoming a carnival.
rules: Deep slate structure and bone-sand replacement planes form the quiet value base.
Copper-orange marks player intervention, reinforcement and approved construction history.
Mint, gold, red and threat raspberry are semantic roles, not decoration.
Color never carries an important state without shape, posture, motion or audio support.
failureModes: Muddy brown monochrome that hides hierarchy.
Orange applied everywhere until authorship loses meaning.
Enemy and player semantic colors sharing the same focal geometry.
acceptance: Grayscale preserves function, orientation and state.
CVD transforms preserve critical distinctions.
Semantic coverage remains within declared caps.

architectureAndFortress.purpose: Make the fortress feel like a persistent collective machine and a personal home.
architectureAndFortress.deepReason: The fortress is the visual protagonist and the player's durable identity. Architecture must therefore combine shared structural logic with visible layers of personal decisions, victories and repairs.
rules: Major architecture uses standardized bays, buttresses, service spines and readable circulation.
Personal history occupies replaceable skins, trophies, repair bands, attachments and spatial composition.
Defensive direction, safe circulation and critical infrastructure remain obvious from the game camera.
Old damage history may be commemorated without making a restored fortress look currently broken.
failureModes: A complete map exported as one decorative mesh.
Architecture so irregular that navigation and build sockets become ambiguous.
Cosmetic clutter hiding threats, routes or interaction zones.
acceptance: A player can identify home, workshop, defense line and objective hierarchy quickly.
Multiple fortresses share a civilization while retaining owner identity.
Thirty repeated modules form rhythm rather than cloning noise.

environmentAndBiomes.purpose: Let expeditions reveal distinct resource histories without breaking the common civilization grammar.
environmentAndBiomes.deepReason: Exploration should expand strategic possibility. Biomes become meaningful when their materials, hazards and recovered technologies visibly explain what the player can bring back to the fortress.
rules: Each biome has one dominant environmental force, one material response and one recoverable technology family.
Natural forms remain broad and stylized; human salvage follows the same joint and semantic grammar as the fortress.
Local color shifts affect neutrals and atmosphere, never the universal interaction, warning, critical or threat roles.
Navigation silhouettes remain calmer than combat silhouettes.
failureModes: Biome identity reduced to a color filter.
Unrelated art styles presented as separate expeditions.
Dense foliage, fog or debris obscuring causal combat information.
acceptance: A screenshot communicates biome force and available salvage opportunity.
Recovered modules visibly belong to both their origin biome and the shared fortress technology.
Combat readability survives the adverse biome lighting profile.

playerBuildables.purpose: Make every placed defense feel owned, understandable and worth iterating.
playerBuildables.deepReason: The core verb is preparing and testing a defense. Buildables must act as legible hypotheses: the player should predict what they do, observe why they fail and know what to change next.
rules: Friendly chassis, rear service access and copper authorship cues identify player ownership.
Active direction and effect origin remain obvious from the primary silhouette.
Upgrades preserve the base object's identity and add one larger functional module rather than many small decorations.
Damage follows named load paths and exposes actionable weaknesses.
failureModes: Cosmetic uniqueness that makes function ambiguous.
Upgrade tiers becoming larger noise piles.
Friendly devices using hostile forward wedges or threat color.
acceptance: Function and orientation are recognized in one second.
The player can identify the failed component after an assault.
Variants remain a coherent kit at 1, 30 and 100 copies.

objectivesAndInteractables.purpose: Create protected focal points with unmistakable service access and state.
objectivesAndInteractables.deepReason: Objectives organize attention and cooperation. Their construction must communicate value, vulnerability and repair opportunity without requiring text or color-only instructions.
rules: Objectives use protected radial or nested forms within a grounded service chassis.
The interaction socket is complete when usable, open or crossed when disabled.
Valuable cores breathe slowly and remain visually contained until a causal failure exposes them.
Service-side access and threat-side protection are distinct.
failureModes: Flat boxes with emissive color as the only objective cue.
Cores so bright that surrounding damage becomes unreadable.
Symmetric access points that confuse safe interaction orientation.
acceptance: Players identify value, access side and current state without text.
Critical exposure is visible but does not occlude attackers.
Cooperative repair positions remain spatially legible.

enemiesAndThreats.purpose: Oppose the fortress grammar while remaining readable, stylized and non-gory.
enemiesAndThreats.deepReason: Enemies must create pressure without visual ambiguity. The standard rôdeur is a zombie, not a hostile machine: violet biological identity, face-led posture and stateful locomotion make the horde memorable while role-specific massing keeps every counter readable and fair.
rules: Every enemy leads with a role-specific hostile primary mass; the standard rôdeur leads with a bowed visible zombie head, hunched torso and reaching open hand rather than a visor or giant fist.
Standard horde biology uses deep eggplant and desaturated plum as a persistent faction family; raspberry remains a bounded forward facial or offensive cue, never the whole body.
Biology remains primary on zombies. Hardened growth may express frontier adaptation, but armor chassis, service panels, copper repairs and mechanical joints are forbidden.
The standard rôdeur must remain visibly weaker and narrower than the wall-attacking brute: medium open hands, no heroic stance and no wall-breaking mass.
Enemy asymmetry may reach 0.30 because it communicates behavior, but locomotion and hit volume remain honest.
Threat raspberry is confined to forward sensory or offensive zones.
Damage exposes non-gory dry fiber or mineral-biological structure through one major causal break and must also change posture, limb function and gait.
failureModes: Enemies resembling friendly buildables or Roblox avatars.
The standard zombie reading as a robot, mech, armored golem, brute or mascot.
Thin limbs and noisy shells disappearing in hordes.
Player-style copper repair bands implying friendly ownership.
Purple used as neon decoration or as the sole carrier of hostile identity or health state.
acceptance: The standard rôdeur reads as a violet zombie in one second with emission and color removed.
Threat direction, attack family and integrity state read in silhouette and posture.
Enemy types remain separable in a dense horde.
Damage state never depends on gore, texture noise or color alone.

avatarsAndCharacters.purpose: Preserve Roblox identity while integrating characters into the frontier culture.
avatarsAndCharacters.deepReason: The GDD values social expression and platform identity. The DA should frame the avatar as the capable author of the fortress, not replace it with an overdesigned proprietary silhouette.
rules: Preserve recognizable Roblox body proportions, face readability and equipped identity.
Wearable technology uses broad harnesses, protected tools and modular repair attachments.
Role readability comes from one large tool silhouette and one bounded color cue.
Faces remain expressive, stylized and readable without photoreal skin treatment.
failureModes: Armor swallowing avatar identity.
Tiny costume greebles competing with held tools.
Faction colors replacing personal expression.
acceptance: A player recognizes their avatar and role simultaneously.
Social screenshots preserve distinct player identities.
Equipment remains readable on mobile and in cooperative clusters.

damageStatesAndRepair.purpose: Make every failure understandable, recoverable and visually linked to the next action.
damageStatesAndRepair.deepReason: Every Failure Teaches is the current priority hypothesis. Visual damage must therefore behave as causal information, not spectacle or generic deterioration.
rules: Damaged introduces one major break, displacement or open joint along the weakest declared path.
Critical widens the same chain with a second major break, exposed core or stopped posture.
Repair reverses the visible sequence and may leave one clean historical intervention marker.
The invariant chassis, pivot, footprint and interaction anchor survive every state.
failureModes: Independent state models with changed proportions or component identity.
Random crack networks, universal sparks or color-only health.
Repair magic that closes damage without a visible mechanical sequence.
acceptance: Players order intact, damaged and critical states without labels.
A reviewer can name the initial failure cause.
The repair animation shows an intelligible inverse transformation.

vfxAndLighting.purpose: Amplify cause, direction and severity while preserving the object and battlefield.
vfxAndLighting.deepReason: Spectacle supports emotion only if it does not hide the information players need to learn and coordinate. The warm frontier needs atmospheric beauty, but gameplay light remains an evidence system.
rules: Impact effects use wedges, arcs and two or three large fragments aligned with incoming force.
Smoke stays thin, short and offset from the interaction or target center.
Emissive areas remain protected and local; world lighting carries mood, not state truth alone.
Warm practical pools support home and repair; cool environmental light preserves frontier scale.
failureModes: Particle fog, full-screen bloom or sparks covering the target.
Lighting tuned to one hero shot.
Every object emitting cyan until interaction hierarchy disappears.
acceptance: Cause and direction remain readable on the effect's peak frame.
Assets pass all four lighting profiles.
Disabling particles does not remove state comprehension.

animationAndMotion.purpose: Make machinery feel heavy, repairable and intentional while keeping motion as a semantic cue.
animationAndMotion.deepReason: Motion can communicate readiness, targeting and failure faster than texture. Industrial discipline provides clear pivots and staging; Salvaged identity adds slight mechanical character without instability.
rules: Primary mechanical motion uses anticipation, one readable axis and a firm settle.
Ready motion is slow and stable; warning motion becomes irregular; critical motion stops or collapses.
Repaired modules may have a slightly different damping profile but share the same functional timing.
No idle motion may resemble threat targeting or interaction readiness accidentally.
failureModes: Constant fidgeting that destroys calm massing.
Wobbly salvage motion implying poor construction everywhere.
Multiple small moving parts obscuring the important axis.
acceptance: State can be identified from motion alone in a short clip.
Pivots and clearances match the canonical component structure.
Motion remains readable at the target mobile distance.

uiSignageAndWorldCues.purpose: Use spatial and shape language before text to guide building, repair and combat.
uiSignageAndWorldCues.deepReason: Mobile-first interaction and international accessibility favor visual grammar. World cues should feel manufactured by the frontier culture while remaining cleaner than decorative signage.
rules: Use complete sockets, chevrons, brackets, rings and footprints as primary world cues.
Text is optional, large and supplemental; invented microtext is forbidden.
Placement previews inherit the real footprint, front direction and semantic role.
Copper indicates authored construction; mint indicates available interaction; gold and red indicate severity.
failureModes: Decorative labels or fictional alphabets carrying required meaning.
UI color fields detached from the object's physical interaction zone.
Placement ghosts that lie about collision or orientation.
acceptance: A first-time player can locate the actionable zone without reading.
World cues remain coherent in grayscale.
UI and object state never contradict each other.

cameraCompositionAndMobile.purpose: Preserve causality, scale and visual beauty under the real gameplay camera.
cameraCompositionAndMobile.deepReason: A direction that only works in close hero renders is not the game's art direction. Mobile screen space, elevated camera angles and dense defense scenes define the actual aesthetic constraints.
rules: Primary forms survive at sixty studs and tertiary details are expendable below their screen-space band.
Top surfaces carry simplified orientation and ownership cues for elevated cameras.
Hero compositions preserve the same front, footprint and state reads used in gameplay.
Foreground effects and architecture must not hide cause, target, direction or priority.
failureModes: Beauty dependent on eye-level closeups.
Important cues placed only on hidden side faces.
Dense silhouettes merging into one dark band in repeated defense lines.
acceptance: Near, mid, far, landscape and portrait views pass.
One-second function and state tests pass on the weakest supported viewport.
Hero art remains honest to gameplay geometry.

socialPersistenceAndCosmetics.purpose: Turn visual progression into personal and shared memory without selling ambiguity or power.
socialPersistenceAndCosmetics.deepReason: The GDD positions the fortress as identity and museum. Cosmetics should celebrate authorship, mastery and cooperation while leaving gameplay function and state universally readable.
rules: Cosmetics modify approved skins, repair signatures, trophy mounts and bounded secondary modules.
Core silhouette, interaction, threat, warning, critical and collision cues remain invariant.
Historical repairs, expedition materials and social trophies can accumulate in designated calm zones.
Prestige reflects creation or contribution and never imitates combat power.
failureModes: Paid skins hiding function or damage.
Cosmetic rarity encoded with critical or interaction colors.
Unlimited trophy clutter destroying fortress readability.
acceptance: Another player recognizes function before cosmetic theme.
Owner history is visible without requiring inventory inspection.
Social screenshots show both shared civilization and personal authorship.

proceduralGenerationAndVariation.purpose: Produce scalable variety without identity drift or probabilistic invention.
proceduralGenerationAndVariation.deepReason: The workflow depends on automation. Variation must operate inside locked ranges so many assets feel authored while remaining reproducible, reviewable and compatible with Roblox integration.
rules: Generators choose only from approved chassis modules, joint families, material roles and repair reasons.
Variation seed, canon hash, constitution hash and selected repair narrative are recorded.
Primary silhouette and gameplay anchors never vary without a canon revision.
Wear, fastener grouping and tertiary repair shape may vary only within declared bounds.
failureModes: The generator filling unspecified space with decoration.
Random asymmetry or material assignment.
Variants requiring unique meshes or textures when instancing should be preserved.
acceptance: Repeated seed produces semantically identical output.
Different seeds remain visibly in the same family.
Every generated choice can be traced to an allowed rule.

marketingAndKeyArt.purpose: Communicate the real game promise through a memorable fortress identity.
marketingAndKeyArt.deepReason: Marketing must show the same causal fantasy players receive: a personal fortress, an intelligent threat and visible adaptation. A generic shooter image would erase the product's strongest differentiation.
rules: The fortress or a player-authored defense occupies the compositional authority.
Show one visible problem, one adapted solution and one readable incoming threat.
Use warm intervention against cool frontier scale to create emotional focus.
Preserve actual asset proportions, colors and state language.
failureModes: Generic armed avatar hero shot with the fortress as background.
Excessive destruction that implies irreversible loss or gore.
Concept art detail density impossible in gameplay.
acceptance: The image communicates build, test, learn and improve without explanatory copy.
Assets shown are production-faithful.
The emotional tone is pressured, inventive, social and hopeful.

performanceAndRepetition.purpose: Keep the direction beautiful and readable when the game contains real quantities of assets.
performanceAndRepetition.deepReason: The fortress fantasy depends on repeated modules and horde pressure. A style that works for one prop but collapses at thirty or one hundred copies is aesthetically and technically invalid.
rules: Reuse MeshIds, trim logic, material families and standardized modules.
Variation occurs at kit composition, repair cluster and placement levels before unique geometry.
Small repeated details lose shadows and tertiary geometry first.
Group value rhythm alternates calm chassis masses and bounded semantic focal points.
failureModes: Every copy carrying a unique texture or mesh.
Repeated copper accents forming an uninterrupted noisy stripe.
Shadows and transparency multiplying without measured benefit.
acceptance: Scenes at 1, 30 and 100 copies preserve function and state hierarchy.
Instance reuse and texture memory remain within budget.
The group reads as an authored defense system rather than cloned clutter.

productionRules: Salvaged Frontier is the sole identity authority; Industrial Toy Defense is never a second visual theme.
Every production asset must bind this exact constitution ID and SHA-256 in addition to its exact visual canon.
The standardized chassis is designed first; repair history is applied only after function, silhouette and construction pass.
Every visible adaptation requires one allowed reason: replacement, reinforcement, sealing or rerouting.
Anything not explicitly variable remains stable across regeneration, state, variant and reimport.
No asset enters production from prose alone: all required multimodal boards and human approval remain mandatory.
A beautiful result that violates function, causality, mobile readability or performance is rejected.
Changing this constitution requires a versioned founder decision and invalidates affected evidence hashes.

requiredViews: Front, back, left, right, top, bottom and both three-quarter views.
Canonical elevated gameplay camera in landscape and portrait.
Black silhouette, flat albedo, detail-band and material-isolation passes.
All states side by side with invariant component annotations.
requiredContexts: Four canonical lighting profiles and both light and dark semantic backgrounds.
Mobile near, mid and far distances with exact camera calibration.
Golden Scene Studio readback and a named low-tier physical mobile session.
perceptualQuestions: What is it, which way does it act and who owns it?
What changed, what caused the change and what should the player do next?
Which visible feature expresses Salvaged Frontier identity without weakening the gameplay icon?
Would the object remain beautiful and understandable if color, particles and tertiary texture were removed?
reopenConditions: A sixth asset requires a new shape, joint, material, semantic color or repair reason.
Human testing cannot recognize function, orientation or state at the declared distance.
The 1, 30 or 100 repetition scene becomes noisy, muddy or technically over budget.
The selected aesthetic cannot support a required biome, character, social expression or gameplay state.
A production constraint forces silent mutation of a canonical invariant.
